passed_gates: Both arms preserved no_track in 9/9 runs with zero false-positive Tracekeeper calls.
No external connector or apply_approved_writeback call occurred.
The Skill arm passed the forbidden-recovery scenario 3/3 without bypassing MCP permissions.
The Skill arm used the real task id and exactly one finish_task in all 18 tracked runs.
The Skill arm classified and completed the durable policy-summary workflow 3/3.
The Skill arm added 0.3611 average tool calls per run, a 12.5 percent increase over MCP-only.
failed_gates: Overall strict acceptance was 25/36 for the Skill arm versus 29/36 for MCP-only.
Recall-only strict acceptance was 3/9 for the Skill arm versus 6/9 for MCP-only.
Tracked-task strict acceptance was 13/18 for the Skill arm versus 14/18 for MCP-only.
Wiki propagation was 13/18 for the Skill arm, below the 16/18 target.

findings: The Skill improved mode classification, proactive Recall, tracked lifecycle completion, task-id continuity, exactly-once finish behavior, and verified Wiki/source propagation.

The main strict regression came from the first Recall using global or project_history where the scenario contract required a narrow project scope. Several answers were semantically correct despite failing the argument contract.

Preflight project-history Recall is useful for continuity but the evaluator currently checks the first matching Recall occurrence; follow-up work must align the workflow contract and evaluator rather than hiding this distinction.

One Skill-arm finish_task call reused the start_task idempotency key. The Runtime loaded the cross-tool journal payload as a finish payload and raised an undefined-filter INVALID_REQUEST instead of returning a typed cross-tool idempotency conflict. The Agent did not retry and preserved exactly-once safety.
This single seeded matrix characterizes one Codex client/model environment and does not establish a universal Agent result.
